rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The reply changed: the student-TIN test is now person.tin, but without person.itin_applied, which the project accepts (p970 p. 11: "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return"; ruled in round 1); by reading, a student whose ITIN was applied for by the due date and issued gets no credit from the candidate (no such record in the sample). It still omits f8863.paid, the return-level screen that precedes person.edu, so the candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the student's answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5): its refusal declaration on person.edu_over is read first, an answer the source does not need when no expenses were paid for anyone (the quoted p. 2 sentence). Generated 47 (round 2's candidate-shows-skipped, the taxpayer with no TIN) now agrees. Its edu_over refusal matches the reworded question (BUG-0197). The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); no record in the sample isolates it this round. Stage 21 re-check: the reply restructured its gates (a shared person.h_edu_base of person.edu, person.edu_1098t and person.tin, the worksheet line read directly from the aqee definition) with the same logic as round 3, so the ruling stands. Its edu_over refusal matches the reworded question (BUG-0197). Generated 47 (round 2's candidate-shows-skipped, the taxpayer with no TIN) now agrees. Its edu_over refusal matches the reworded question (BUG-0197). rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit: "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The reply changed: the student-TIN test is now person.tin, but without person.itin_applied, which the project accepts (p970 p. 11: "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return"; ruled in round 1); by reading, a student whose ITIN was applied for by the due date and issued gets no credit from the candidate (no such record in the sample). It still omits f8863.paid, the return-level screen that precedes person.edu, so the candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the student's answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5): its refusal declaration on person.edu_over is read first, an answer the source does not need when no expenses were paid for anyone (the quoted p. 2 sentence). Generated 47 (round 2's candidate-shows-skipped, the taxpayer with no TIN) now agrees. Its edu_over refusal matches the reworded question (BUG-0197). The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); no record in the sample isolates it this round. Lines 28 to 30 carry no refusal declaration, so on stage19.refuse.period_over_person the project refuses at edu_over_refused and the candidate shows an amount on a return its own line 27 refuses: scope on that kind. Stage 21 re-check: the reply restructured its gates (a shared person.h_edu_base of person.edu, person.edu_1098t and person.tin, the worksheet line read directly from the aqee definition) with the same logic as round 3, so the ruling stands. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)", and Student qualifications: "5. Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." i8863 p. 2: "You may be able to claim an education credit if you, your spouse, or a dependent you claim on your tax return was a student enrolled at or attending an eligible educational institution." The reply changed: the student-TIN test is now person.tin, but without person.itin_applied, which the project accepts (p970 p. 11: "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return"; ruled in round 1); by reading, a student whose ITIN was applied for by the due date and issued gets no credit from the candidate (no such record in the sample). It still omits f8863.paid, the return-level screen that precedes person.edu, so the candidate-unknown records are returns with f8863.paid no, where the interview never asks the student's answers (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5): its refusal declaration on person.edu_over is read first, an answer the source does not need when no expenses were paid for anyone (the quoted p. 2 sentence). Generated 47 (round 2's candidate-shows-skipped, the taxpayer with no TIN) now agrees. Its edu_over refusal matches the reworded question (BUG-0197). The worksheet arithmetic is the project's aqee definition. Lines 27 to 30 also omit the filers' TIN test (household.all_tin, amb.2025.edu_filer_tin, owner decision D7(a)); no record in the sample isolates it this round. Lines 28 to 30 carry no refusal declaration, so on stage19.refuse.period_over_person the project refuses at edu_over_refused and the candidate shows an amount on a return its own line 27 refuses: scope on that kind. The candidate copies the Schedule C line 31 total; the project copies person.sc_total (sc.result) and refuses at person.se_screened, the worksheet with self-employment income not on a Schedule C. The project-refuses are that cited screen (classm.f5695.2 and .2.deepseek, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen true, and the partial records built on them, whose returns complete because the worksheet is not reached; classm.asset.3, classm.carloan.2, classm.f8959.1 on refused returns). The project-unknown records are persons with no Schedule C, where the interview never asks se_screen and the SEP worksheet is not reached (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5): evaluation order, not a defect (round-2 note). No value differs. Stage 21 re-check: the reply's expression for this line and the project's line are unchanged from Stage 19 round 3 (the Stage 21 subject changes only the Form 1099-R totals and the Form 5329 block), and the new triage kinds are the same kinds over the larger sample (the Stage 21 fixtures added). The project refusals are its cited se_screened screen and the at-risk refusal (classm.asset.3; classm.f5695.2.deepseek); the project-unknown records ask se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C; the candidate refusals are other forms' cited refusals on partial records (classm.g28.2.deepseek partial, scveh low_use). rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). Box 1 is the same on both sides. Line 1e goes to the only person whose Forms W-2 show box 10, or to the taxpayer when nobody's do, on both sides; when both spouses' do, the second now gives it to neither (and refuses, its h_dc_1e_split), where the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6): shown in the taxpayer's line 4 and refused when a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate). The self-employment part is the same on returns the tool completes: the second subtracts the Schedule SE deduction without a Schedule C guard (zero below the $400 floor, so the Schedule C result is used, as the project does when no Schedule SE is filed) and leaves out statutory employee income, which is refused on each Schedule C (sc.statutory). i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Box 1 and the self-employment part are the same on both sides: the self-employment part differs only as person.eic_se does (the project's zero for a person with no Schedule C against the second's $400 floor, and the second's exclusion of statutory employee income, which is refused by sc.statutory), and both use Schedule C profit or loss when no Schedule SE is filed (p503 p. 11, Self-employment earnings, "Include your self-employment earnings in earned income, even if they are less than $400 and you didn't file Schedule SE"). Line 1e goes to the only person on a return that is not joint and to the one spouse whose Forms W-2 show box 10 on both sides. The sides differ only when both spouses' Forms W-2 show box 10: the second counts line 1e in both spouses' earned income, so it counts it twice; the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6), refusing when line 1e is above zero and a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate) and otherwise showing it in the taxpayer's line 4, where it cannot change the credit. i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

For a person with no Schedule C the self-employment items the screen lists (church employee income, clergy, partnership and farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (refused at person.credit). rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. EIC Worksheet B Part 1 for a person filing Schedule SE and Part 2 otherwise on both sides (i1040gi p. 47).

A distribution is refused on both sides (f8606.dist; the second's person.ira_dist_gate).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; f8606 (2025) Part I: "In 2025, did you take a distribution from a traditional IRA, or make a Roth IRA conversion?" Both gates are the distribution answer for a Form 8606 filer; the candidate's filer test includes a distribution with basis that the project screens at retirement.special. No value differs. Candidate refusals and unknowns are inherited placements of its own lines, ruled there: se_screen and rrta (classm.w2.1.deepseek, classm.f5695.2.deepseek on a completed return), plan_screen (classm.dependent.7.deepseek), other forms' refusals reached through its modified AGI (classm.g28.2.deepseek scveh low_use), and ira_excess or ira_age50 asked where the interview does not ask them (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5). Project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (stage16.refuse.ira.both_kinds, stage16.refuse.ira.kbh_short, stage16.refuse.person.ira_over_limit, stage16.refuse.ira.over_comp; p590a p. 35, excess contributions); project-unknown records are partials withholding sav_trad, where the candidate's zero follows from no contribution. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/person.json; 1,323 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 1,839 partial records): 2,573 of 4,425 comparisons agree; 140 candidate-refuses, 1,702 candidate-unknown, 10 project-refuses; on returns the full interview completes: 44 candidate-refuses, 728 candidate-unknown.

The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C and otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c (i1040sse p. 2, line 4c; 'If less than $400 ... you don't owe self-employment tax'), which gives zero for the same person. Church employee income, optional methods, statutory employees and notaries are refused on both sides (person.se_screen, sc.statutory). Otherwise both are Schedule SE lines 10 and 11 added (Schedule SE (2025), line 12).

Both give one-half of this person's Schedule SE line 12 on the computation of person.se_line6. The reply is again built on sc.line31 rather than sc.result; they differ only for a loss with amounts not at risk, which the project refuses at sc.loss_allowed (stage14.refuse.at_risk, the one project refusal; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198"). The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C, so the candidate-unknown records are interview records with no Schedule C where it is not asked (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5) and the candidate-refuses supply se_screen true for a person with no Schedule C (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.2.deepseek and classm.ssb.5 on completed returns, and the partial records built on them; classm.carloan.2, classm.f8959.1 and classm.w2.1.deepseek rrta on refused returns), an answer the interview does not produce for that person (scope on those kinds, as rounds 1 and 2). No value differs. Stage 21 re-check: the reply's expression for this line and the project's line are unchanged from Stage 19 round 3 (the Stage 21 subject changes only the Form 1099-R totals and the Form 5329 block), and the new triage kinds are the same kinds over the larger sample (the Stage 21 fixtures added). Both give one-half of this person's Schedule SE line 12 on the same computation as person.se_line6. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C (person.se_line2 is read by person.se_line6 only under person.has_sc) and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the self-employment items the screen lists (church employee income, clergy, partnership and farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (refused at person.credit). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2 and classm.f5695.2.deepseek, classm.ssb.5 on completed returns, classm.carloan.2, classm.f8959.1 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The published label of this line is "This person's worksheet column (b) total"; the candidate sums tipjob.col_c, column (c), and its note says the pages do not say what the line is, against the label it was given.
